newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bertinotti calls for deal to delay EMU.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bertinotti calls for deal to delay EMU.

text.p: The leader of Italy's far-left Communist Refoundation party said on Thursday that Italy should seek a deal with its European Union partners to delay EMU.

Fausto Bertinotti told state radio RAI that Italy "in concert with the other European countries, should advance a realistic proposal of elasticity, at least in terms of the Maastricht criteria and an extension of the time-scale".
Bertinotti, whose support in parliament ensures the centre-left government's majority, has openly questioned the likelihood of economic and monetary union starting on time in 1999.
He says a delay is inevitable because even Germany, the EU's economic powerhouse, is having trouble meeting the tough qualifying criteria.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi reiterated his commitment to be ready for EMU on schedule in a telephone call with French President Jacques Chirac earlier on Thursday.

Prodi is working on a mini-budget, to be unveiled in the next few weeks, to correct a spending overshoot and keep alive Italy's hopes of founder EMU membership. But he faces opposition from Bertinotti who wants no welfare spending cuts or tax hikes.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told news weekly Panorama in an interview issued ahead of publication on Friday that the centre-left government needed to put Bertinotti in his place.

"Even Bertinotti must be brought to heel," Dini said. "The mini-budget is the first step...Let (the government) make its proposal, including a reduction in public spending, and send it to parliament. With or without Bertinotti. We'll see."
